title: Choose the tracker’s visual world
question: Pick the working surface for your eight-week inference roadmap. Every option stays intentionally focused and minimal.

options.label: Benchmark Ledger
options.lineage: inference benchmark result sheets and lab run logs
options.thesis: Treat the roadmap like a sequence of measured runs whose evidence, not optimism, marks progress.
options.viewport: A slim progress rail anchors a full-width eight-row ledger; the current week opens inline with its deliverables and notes.
options.risk: Can feel clinical if the notes and current-focus treatment do not provide enough warmth.

raised.raise: Weeks receive direct numeric addressing and strong keyboard navigation.
Notes and task state remain editable in place instead of opening a management layer.
Completed work leaves a legible evidence trail rather than disappearing into a percentage.
The current week is unmistakably marked while past work visually recedes.

options.label: Engineer’s Field Log
options.lineage: bound engineering notebooks and annotated runbooks
options.thesis: Each week is a compact field entry: intent, proof produced, and the next operational question.
options.viewport: A quiet index margin sits beside one open weekly log, with completion marks accumulating down the binding edge.
options.risk: The notebook metaphor is familiar and can become decorative if the task controls are not disciplined.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The roadmap becomes eight directly addressable status pages with progress broadcast in a rigid live grid.
options.viewport: A 40-column progress index lists W01–W08; selecting a number reveals that week without changing the grid.
options.case: Strong engineer identification and direct state visibility; loses some calm and prose readability.
options.risk: Can read as retro novelty and constrain longer notes.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Each week is an editable card in a personal stack with a truthful trail back through completed work.
options.viewport: A fixed-proportion week card leads while an exposed stack edge shows all eight stages and completion state.
options.case: Excellent personal-tool character and in-place editing; weaker at whole-roadmap comparison.
options.risk: The fixed card frame can hide cross-week progress on small screens.

options.label: Calendar Pad
options.thesis: Each completed week tears forward through the roadmap.
options.viewport: A large current-week leaf sits above an eight-week date grid.
options.case: The time axis is clear, but the physical-calendar identity obscures portfolio evidence.
options.kept: Past work recedes and the current step receives one unmistakable marker.
options.risk: Completion can feel like discarding work rather than accumulating proof.

options.label: Origami Sequence
options.thesis: Every completed deliverable becomes a visible crease in one continuous transformation.
options.viewport: Eight numbered folds surround the active step and its concrete output.
options.case: Sequence and accumulated progress fit, but the metaphor competes with technical information.
options.kept: Every completed action leaves a visible trace in the final state.
options.risk: A literal fold interaction would add complexity without improving the tracking task.

canonCard.label: Minimal SaaS dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional sidebar, progress cards, and checklist rendered with careful restraint.
canonCard.viewport: Summary cards sit above a two-column weekly task dashboard.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar, but indistinguishable from generic productivity software.
